title: 1 · Sounds, spelling and stress
blurb: Read any Cebuano word with the pronunciation line: the three vowels, ng and mga, the catch, and the stressed syllable.

title: 2 · Greetings and polite words
blurb: Greet people at any time of day, ask how they are, say thanks and please, and address older people politely.

title: 3 · Small words: man, lang, sab, diay
blurb: Use the small words that make Cebuano sound friendly (man, lang, ra, sab, diay, ba, gyud) and put them in the right place.

title: 4 · kini, kana, kadto: this and that
blurb: Point at things in a shop or market: ask what they are, and choose between this, that by you and that over there.

title: 5 · I, you, he, she: ako, ikaw, siya and ang / si
blurb: Say who someone is (a teacher, a student, an American) with ako, ikaw, siya, and the markers si and ang.

title: 6 · Introducing yourself
blurb: Give your name, say where you are from and where you live, give your age, and ask the same back.

title: 7 · Question words: unsa, kinsa, asa, ngano, kanus-a
blurb: Ask what, who, where, why, when and how much, and ask yes-or-no questions with ba.

title: 8 · We, you all, they: kami, kita, kamo, sila
blurb: Choose the right we (with or without the listener), talk to a group, talk about others, and make nouns plural with mga.

title: 9 · My, your, his: nako, akong and ni / sa
blurb: Say whose something is in two ways (akong balay, balay nako), and use ni with names and sa with other nouns.

title: 10 · Describing words and the linker nga
blurb: Describe things (big, small, new, old, hot, cold) with the linker nga, and tell a phrase from a full sentence.

title: 11 · There is, have: naa, aduna, wala
blurb: Say what there is and what you have, ask a shop for something, and say there is none.

title: 12 · How you feel: gigutom ko, kapoy kaayo
blurb: Say you are hungry, thirsty, tired, full or happy, ask how someone feels, and say what hurts.

title: 13 · Numbers: Cebuano and Spanish
blurb: Count things with Cebuano numbers and ka, and say prices and ages with Spanish numbers.

title: 14 · Prices and buying: Tagpila?
blurb: Ask what things cost, understand the answer in Spanish numbers, and ask for a small discount at a market.

title: 15 · Family
blurb: Name the people in your family, say whose relative someone is, and use family titles politely.

title: 16 · Doer-focus verbs 1: mo- (will) and ni- (did)
blurb: Say what you will do and what you did with mo- and ni- verbs, and what you buy, eat or drink with og.

title: 17 · Doer-focus verbs 2: mag- and nag-
blurb: Use mag- and nag- verbs to say what you will do, what you did and what you are doing, and to say "let's".

title: 18 · dili and wala: two words for not
blurb: Choose between dili and wala to say you won't, you didn't, it isn't, or there is none.

title: 19 · Days and the clock: alas tres, Lunes, ugma
blurb: Tell the time with Spanish numbers, name the days, and use today, tomorrow and yesterday with the right verb form.

title: 20 · Want, need, don't: gusto, kinahanglan, ayaw
blurb: Say what you want, need and like, refuse politely, and tell someone not to do something.

title: 21 · Asking politely: palihug and the command form
blurb: Ask people to do things and to give you things, politely, the way Cebuanos soften a request.

title: 22 · Ordering food
blurb: Order at a carinderia, ask what they have, say the food is good, and ask for the total.

title: 23 · Where things are: asa, diri, diha, didto
blurb: Ask where a place is, say where things and people are, and use the right word for here and there.

title: 24 · Directions and jeepneys
blurb: Follow and give simple directions, ride a jeepney, pay your fare and get off where you want.

title: 25 · Thing-focus verbs: -on and gi-
blurb: Talk about doing something to a particular thing: the bananas, this mango, my water.

title: 26 · Place-focus verbs: -an and gi-…-an
blurb: Talk about doing something to a person or a surface: helping someone, writing to someone, washing the dishes.

title: 27 · Comparing: mas, kaysa, pinaka-
blurb: Say that something is bigger, cheaper or tastier than something else, the best of all, or the same.

title: 28 · Can and managed to: maka- and naka-
blurb: Say what you can and can't do, ask if someone can come, and ask whether they have ever been somewhere.
